subject: Launch capacity guarantee + per-token escrow proposal
messages:
From: Natalie Reed <natalie@skylift.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@skylift.ai, Tom Hwang <tom.h@skylift.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity guarantee + pricing question for Q1 launch

Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and the routing options. We need to lock a pricing/commit structure quickly: Skylift is targeting a public launch in mid-Dec with a 90-day marketing ramp. Expected monthly token usage profile (attached) is very lumpy — baseline small, then 3x–6x spikes for campaign-driven days.

Key asks: 
- Can Redwood provide a monthly commit schedule with a step-up option (we want to start small and be able to increase commits mid-contract without re-signing each month)?
- We need a capacity guarantee for launch days (we want a firm burst capacity reservation and an insurance that covers overage so our UI doesn't degrade).
- Procurement wants an escrow-style mechanism: committed funds held as pre-paid credits that are released as usage occurs, with a monthly true-up. This helps finance on our side.

Can you share an initial term structure and any standard language you use for seasonal/launch ramps? I attached our forecast (Skylift_Ramp_Forecast.xlsx).

Also looping in Tom from ops and procurement alias.

Thanks,
Natalie Reed
Head of Product
Skylift.ai

Attachment: Skylift_Ramp_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Natalie Reed <natalie@skylift.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Tom Hwang <tom.h@skylift.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity guarantee + pricing question for Q1 launch

Hi Natalie — great to hear and thanks for the forecast. Short answer: yes, we can support a monthly step-up commit structure and a pre-funded credit model; we also offer an explicit surge/insurance pool to handle short-term bursts. High level proposal below; I'll put a draft term sheet in a follow-up email and loop Rishi (sales director) and Karthik (pricing/solutions) to iterate.

Proposed high-level constructs:
- Monthly step-up commits: client signs a 3-month master schedule with month-by-month committed token buckets (you can increase a bucket with 7-days notice). Increases are additive and effective the first full billing period after notice.
- Pre-funded credits (what procurement is calling escrow): we can hold pre-paid credits in the customer account. Credits are applied to usage daily and reconciled monthly. Unused credits can be returned at contract milestones or applied forward per negotiated true-up terms.
- Surge insurance pool: an add-on pool sized as a percentage of the committed bucket (we typically recommend 50% for launch days). This pool provides automatic cover for bursts up to its size; overage beyond the pool is billed at an overage rate or drawn from remaining pre-paid credits.

A couple of optional guardrails we recommend: 1) a maximum per-day burst multiplier (e.g., 6x committed daily throughput) to allow us to provision headroom; 2) a one-time true-up at month-end for overage/underuse.

I'll send a draft term sheet and pricing bands now.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_TermSheet_v1.pdf (pdf, 85KB)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Natalie Reed <natalie@skylift.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Tom Hwang <tom.h@skylift.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed pricing and monthly true-up flow

Natalie / team — adding a bit more detail on the economics so procurement has something concrete. These are suggested bands; we can tighten with committed volume.

Per-token bands (hosted API, generation tokens):
- Tier A (0 - 250M tokens / month): $0.00095 per token
- Tier B (250M - 750M): $0.00072 per token
- Tier C (750M+): custom enterprise pricing (we can propose $0.00050–0.00060 depending on guaranteed commit)

Monthly true-up flow:
1) You pre-fund a monthly credit bucket equal to agreed committed tokens * listed rate (or an agreed dollar guarantee).
2) Usage is deducted from the bucket daily. Surges first draw from the surge insurance pool (if purchased), then from the bucket.
3) At month end we perform a one-time true-up: if usage > prepaid, invoice the delta; if usage < prepaid we either roll forward credits or issue a refund per the MSA.

Escrow note: we don't use third-party escrow for credits by default, but for enterprise customers we are open to an escrow arrangement where funds are held in a short-term account and released against usage. That would need procurement/legal discussion and a simple addendum.

One operational ask: please confirm expected peak Q1 day token rate (tokens/minute) so Karthik can validate the burst multiplier and capacity reservations.

Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Hwang <tom.h@skylift.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Natalie Reed <natalie@skylift.ai>, procure@skylift.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed pricing and monthly true-up flow

Thanks — attaching the per-day peak estimates and a simple procurement checklist (we've also highlighted preferred language around returns on unused pre-paid credits). Couple clarifications from procurement: 
- We prefer the escrow to be documented as 'pre-funded credits held in Redwood account, refundable if not consumed after a 90-day rolling window' (procurement wants the runway protection).
- For burst sizing, our ops target is ~12M tokens/day peak during a campaign day, which is roughly ~8k tokens/min sustained for 25 minutes.
- Can the surge insurance be set as a fixed dollar pool instead of percentage? That simplifies our finance reconciliation.

Attached: Skylift_Ramp_Forecast.xlsx (updated), Draft_MSA_Redlines.pdf

Tom Hwang
Senior Systems Engineer, Skylift.ai

Subject: Term sheet + next steps (monthly ramp + escrow language)

Natalie / Tom — thanks for the updated numbers. Attached is a concise term sheet that reflects: monthly step-up commit schedule, pre-funded credit model (described as refundable credits after 90 days), optional fixed-dollar surge pool (you'd specify $X per month), and the monthly true-up flow. Highlights: 
- Initial 3-month schedule with ability to increase month buckets with 7 days notice. Decreases require 30 days notice and may be subject to a prorated true-up.
- Surge insurance: proposed fixed-dollar pool = $25,000 / month for launch months; applies before overage billing.
- Per-token bands: Tier A / Tier B / Tier C as discussed.
- Escrow-like language: funds sit as pre-paid credits in account and are refundable if not applied after a rolling 90-day period; legal addendum for a third-party escrow can be added if required.

Next steps: 1) Confirm the $25k surge pool or propose an alternative fixed amount; 2) Procurement to confirm the refundable-credit 90-day window; 3) If agreed, I'll issue a redline-ready term sheet and DocuSign link for a short MSA addendum.

I'm attaching the PDF term sheet and adding a docusign link for convenience. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk the economics.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_TermSheet_v1.pdf, Redwood_TermSheet_v1-annotated.docx (term highlights), DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abcd-termsheet
